chunks.section: Item 4. Advisory Business > 4.2 Advisory Services and Strategies
chunks.text: Wrenholt Pryce provides investment management services exclusively in U.S. dollar denominated fixed income. The Firm manages separately managed accounts ("separate accounts") for public pension plans and insurance companies, and it sponsors and manages one private commingled fund. The Firm offers three strategies: - **Core Fixed Income.** Investment grade portfolios of U.S. Treasury, agency, agency mortgage-backed, investment grade corporate, taxable municipal and asset-backed securities, managed against a broad investment grade aggregate index chosen by the client. Portfolio duration is generally kept within 0.5 years of the duration of the index. - **Long Duration Credit.** Portfolios of long maturity investment grade corporate and taxable municipal bonds, together with U.S. Treasury STRIPS and Treasury futures used to manage duration and key rate exposures, for defined benefit pension plans seeking to align the interest rate sensitivity of plan assets with that of plan liabilities. Target duration, generally between 12 and 16 years, is set with the client and its actuary or investment consultant. - **Insurance Core.** Investment grade portfolios for insurance company general accounts, managed to client objectives for book yield, risk-based capital, NAIC designation mix, asset and liability duration, and the timing of realized gains and losses. Insurance Core portfolios may hold privately placed corporate notes issued in reliance on Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933. The Firm does not sponsor or participate in wrap fee programs and does not provide financial planning, asset allocation advice across asset classes, or advice to individuals.

chunks.section: Item 4. Advisory Business > 4.3 Client Guidelines and Restrictions
chunks.text: Each separate account is managed under an investment management agreement ("IMA") and written investment guidelines negotiated with the client. Guidelines typically specify permitted sectors, minimum average and per-issue credit quality, the maximum allocation to below investment grade securities (often zero for public pension clients and up to 5% for insurance clients), issuer and industry concentration limits, duration bands, permitted derivatives and the reference index. Clients may prohibit investment in specific issuers, industries or countries. Several public pension clients are subject to state statutes requiring divestment from issuers named on lists maintained by a state agency; when a client provides such a list, the Firm codes it as a hard restriction in its order management system within five business days of receipt. Guideline limits are measured at the time of purchase unless the guidelines provide otherwise.

chunks.text: The Firm sponsors Wrenholt Pryce Long Duration Credit Fund, L.P. (the "Commingled Fund" or the "Fund"), a Delaware limited partnership that commenced operations in July 2014 and pursues the Long Duration Credit strategy. Wrenholt Pryce Fund GP LLC, an affiliate of the Firm, is the Fund's general partner. Interests in the Fund are offered privately to investors that are "qualified purchasers," and the Fund relies on the exclusion from the definition of investment company in Section 3(c)(7) of the Investment Company Act of 1940. Quillfield Fund Services LLC serves as the Fund's administrator, Ostrander Keel Trust Company, N.A. serves as its custodian, and Marrick Tolland LLP serves as its independent auditor. Investors in the Fund cannot impose individual investment restrictions. The general partner monitors investment by benefit plan investors, as defined in Section 3(42) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 ("ERISA"), so that those investors hold less than 25% of the value of each class of interests and the Fund's assets are not treated as plan assets.

chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.4 Billing
chunks.text: Separate account fees are billed quarterly in arrears based on the average of the three month-end market values of the account during the quarter, including accrued interest. Market values are determined by the Firm under its Valuation Policy and reconciled monthly to the records of the client's custodian. The Firm delivers invoices within 15 business days after quarter end, and payment is due within 30 days after the invoice date. Fees for a partial quarter are prorated by the number of days the account was under management. The Firm does not deduct fees directly from separate accounts; every separate account client pays by invoice. When a client requests, the Firm aggregates accounts of the same plan sponsor, or of insurance companies under common control, for purposes of applying breakpoints.

chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.1 Methods of Analysis
chunks.text: The Firm combines top-down and bottom-up analysis. The Investment Policy Committee, chaired by the Chief Investment Officer, meets at least monthly to set ranges for duration, yield curve positioning and sector allocation based on its view of growth, inflation, monetary policy and relative value. Within those ranges, portfolio managers select securities based on fundamental credit research. The Firm's credit research team, led by Rafael Denholm, Head of Credit Research, assigns an internal credit rating to every corporate and taxable municipal issuer approved for purchase, based on business risk, leverage and cash flow coverage, liquidity, covenant protection and, for municipal issuers, the revenue pledge and legal structure. Approved issuers are reviewed at least annually and upon material events. Structured and mortgage-backed securities are evaluated with prepayment, default and loss-severity models. The risk management function, led by the Chief Risk Officer, measures each portfolio's duration, key rate duration, spread duration, tracking error, issuer concentration and liquidity, and runs rate shock and spread widening scenarios. For Long Duration Credit clients, the Firm also measures the portfolio's hedge ratio against the liability cash flows provided by the client or its actuary.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.2 Investment Strategies
chunks.text: The Firm's strategies emphasize sector allocation and issuer selection over large deviations in duration. Long Duration Credit portfolios use Treasury futures and, where guidelines permit, cleared interest rate swaps to adjust duration without selling cash bonds; the notional exposure of these instruments may create economic leverage. Insurance Core portfolios are managed with a buy-and-maintain orientation because realized gains and losses affect the statutory income of insurance clients. The Firm does not engage in securities lending on behalf of clients.

chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.3 Risk of Loss
chunks.text: Investing in securities involves risk of loss that clients should be prepared to bear. A portfolio managed by the Firm may lose value or underperform its reference index, and the Firm does not guarantee any return or the achievement of any liability-matching objective. The principal risks are summarized below; the list is not exhaustive.

chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.4 Principal Risks
chunks.text: **Interest rate risk.** Fixed income prices generally fall when interest rates rise. The longer the duration of a portfolio, the more sensitive it is to rate changes; a Long Duration Credit portfolio with a duration of 14 years would be expected to lose approximately 14% of its value if yields rose one percentage point across the curve, before accounting for income and convexity. **Credit risk.** An issuer may fail to make interest or principal payments when due, or its creditworthiness may deteriorate. Credit rating downgrades can reduce prices and, for insurance clients, increase required statutory capital. **Spread risk.** Yield spreads over Treasury securities can widen because of economic conditions or investor demand, reducing prices even where issuer fundamentals are unchanged. **Liquidity risk.** Fixed income markets are dealer markets, and dealer capacity to hold inventory can decline sharply in periods of stress. The Firm may be unable to sell a position at a price close to its carrying value, particularly for long maturity, small issue or privately placed securities. **Call, prepayment and extension risk.** Callable bonds may be redeemed and mortgages prepaid when rates fall, forcing reinvestment at lower yields; when rates rise, prepayments may slow and extend duration. **Private placement risk.** Privately placed notes held in Insurance Core portfolios are not registered, trade infrequently and are subject to resale restrictions. Their values are determined by the Firm using the matrix methodology described in its Valuation Policy and may differ from the price that could be realized in a sale. **Below investment grade risk.** Where guidelines permit, securities rated below investment grade carry a higher risk of default and greater price volatility, and securities downgraded after purchase may be held when

Cleared derivatives expose the account to the risk of its clearing member. **Valuation risk.** Many fixed income securities are valued using evaluated prices from pricing services, dealer quotations or models rather than transaction prices. Values used by the Firm for reporting and fee calculation may differ from the prices at which securities could be sold and from the values reported by a client's custodian. **Rating agency and NAIC designation risk.** The capital requirements of insurance clients depend on ratings and NAIC designations assigned by third parties, which may change in ways that increase capital charges or require sales. **Operational and cybersecurity risk.** Failures of systems, vendors or processes, including cyberattacks, could disrupt trading, compromise confidential information or result in losses. The Firm maintains a business continuity plan and an information security program, but no plan can eliminate these risks.

chunks.section: Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading > 11.1 Code of Ethics
chunks.text: The Firm has adopted a Code of Ethics under Rule 204A-1 under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act"). The Code sets standards of business conduct based on the Firm's fiduciary duty, requires compliance with the federal securities laws, and governs personal trading, gifts and entertainment, political contributions and the handling of material nonpublic information. All employees are treated as access persons. Each employee must acknowledge the Code on hire, annually and upon each amendment. A copy of the Code is available to clients and prospective clients on request to the Chief Compliance Officer.

chunks.section: Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading > 11.2 Personal Trading
chunks.text: Employees must obtain pre-clearance from Compliance before trading covered securities in their personal accounts, must report their holdings and transactions, and must observe a minimum holding period. Employees may not purchase individual corporate, municipal, asset-backed or privately placed debt securities for personal accounts; transactions in U.S. Treasury securities, open-end mutual funds not advised by the Firm and exchange-traded funds are permitted subject to the Code. Employees may invest in the Commingled Fund with the prior approval of the Chief Compliance Officer on the same terms as other investors, except that the management fee is waived. Because employees could benefit from the performance of the Fund, the Firm allocates investment opportunities under the procedures described in Item 12 without regard to employee investment.

chunks.section: Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading > 11.3 Cross Trades
chunks.text: The Firm may effect a cross trade between two client accounts, in which one account sells a security to another, only when the portfolio manager has determined that the transaction is in the best interest of both accounts and consistent with each account's guidelines; the Chief Compliance Officer or the Deputy Chief Compliance Officer has approved the transaction in advance; and the transaction is executed at the current evaluated price supplied by the Firm's independent primary pricing service. Neither the Firm nor any affiliate receives a commission, markup or other compensation in connection with a cross trade. Cross trades are not effected for any account whose IMA or governing law prohibits them.

When an issuer is placed on the restricted list, the Firm may be unable to buy or sell that issuer's securities for client accounts for a period of time, which could disadvantage clients.

chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.1 Selection of Broker-Dealers
chunks.text: The Firm has discretion to select the broker-dealers through which transactions are executed for discretionary accounts. The Firm executes fixed income transactions with dealers on its approved counterparty list, which is maintained by the Best Execution Committee. In selecting a dealer, the Firm considers the net price available, the dealer's willingness to commit capital in the size required, its knowledge of the security, the likelihood of execution, settlement capability and financial condition. For most investment grade transactions, traders solicit competitive quotations from multiple dealers by voice or through electronic request-for-quote platforms; for large or illiquid positions, the Firm may negotiate with a single dealer to limit information leakage. The Best Execution Committee, chaired by the Chief Operating Officer, meets quarterly to review execution quality, including transaction cost analysis prepared by an independent vendor that compares execution prices with evaluated prices at the time of trade, the use of electronic platforms, dealer concentration and settlement failures.

chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.2 Research and Other Soft Dollar Benefits
chunks.text: The Firm does not use client brokerage to obtain research or other products or services, and it has no soft dollar arrangements. Fixed income securities are generally traded on a principal basis at net prices, and the Firm pays for research, market data and analytical services from its own resources.

chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.3 Brokerage for Client Referrals

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.4 Directed Brokerage and Diverse Broker-Dealer Programs
chunks.text: The Firm does not generally permit clients to direct brokerage. Several public pension clients encourage the use of minority-owned, women-owned and veteran-owned broker-dealers, and the Firm includes qualified firms of this type on its approved counterparty list. Where a client's guidelines establish a utilization goal, the Firm seeks to meet it only to the extent consistent with best execution; such trades may not be aggregated and may receive less favorable execution.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.5 Aggregation and Allocation
chunks.text: The Firm may aggregate orders for multiple accounts when it believes aggregation is consistent with its duty to seek best execution. Before an aggregated order is placed, the portfolio manager records the intended allocation in the order management system. If an aggregated order is completely filled, it is allocated according to that pre-allocation; if it is partially filled, it is allocated pro rata based on the pre-allocated amounts, subject to minimum denomination and minimum lot size considerations. New issue allotments are allocated pro rata based on indications recorded before the allotment is received. Each account participating in an aggregated order receives the average price for the order. Any departure from the pre-allocation requires the written approval of the Chief Compliance Officer or the Deputy Chief Compliance Officer.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.6 Trade Errors
chunks.text: The Firm seeks to correct trade errors promptly after discovery so that the affected account is placed in the position it would have occupied had the error not occurred. The Firm reimburses the account for any loss resulting from an error for which the Firm is responsible, and any gain remains in the account. Errors and corrections are documented and reviewed by Compliance.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 13. Review of Accounts > 13.1 Ongoing Review
chunks.text: Portfolio managers review their accounts daily. The order management system checks each proposed trade against coded guideline restrictions before execution, and Compliance reviews post-trade exception reports each business day. The Chief Risk Officer distributes weekly risk reports, and the Investment Policy Committee reviews all strategies monthly. The Chief Investment Officer and the Chief Risk Officer conduct a formal review of each separate account at least quarterly, and upon any material change in a client's guidelines, liabilities or cash flow needs.

chunks.text: Separate account clients receive written quarterly reports showing holdings, transactions, performance against the reference index, portfolio characteristics and market commentary. Insurance Core clients also receive monthly reports formatted to support statutory accounting, including book value, amortized cost, NAIC designations and realized gains and losses by lot. Long Duration Credit clients receive quarterly liability hedge ratio reports. Investors in the Commingled Fund receive monthly net asset value statements from the administrator, quarterly investment reports from the Firm and annual audited financial statements.

chunks.section: Item 14. Client Referrals and Other Compensation > 14.1 Compensation for Client Referrals
chunks.text: The Firm does not directly or indirectly compensate any person who is not a supervised person for client referrals, and it does not engage placement agents or third-party solicitors to obtain mandates from government entities.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 14. Client Referrals and Other Compensation > 14.2 Economic Benefits Received
chunks.text: The Firm does not receive economic benefits, such as sales awards or prizes, from any non-client in connection with its advisory services. Dealers occasionally provide Firm personnel with market commentary and invitations to industry events; these are subject to the gifts and entertainment provisions of the Code of Ethics.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 15. Custody > 15.1 Separate Accounts
chunks.text: Separate account assets are held by qualified custodians selected and engaged by each client. The Firm has no authority to withdraw client funds or securities, other than to instruct custodians to settle transactions against payment, and it does not deduct fees from separate accounts. Clients receive statements directly from their custodians at least quarterly and should compare them with the Firm's reports.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 15. Custody > 15.2 Commingled Fund
chunks.text: Because an affiliate of the Firm serves as general partner, the Firm is deemed to have custody of the Commingled Fund's assets. The Fund's assets are held by Ostrander Keel Trust Company, N.A., a qualified custodian. The Firm complies with the custody rule by having the Fund audited annually by Marrick Tolland LLP, an independent public accountant registered with and subject to regular inspection by the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, and by distributing audited financial statements prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles to all investors within 120 days after the end of the Fund's fiscal year, which ends December 31.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 16. Investment Discretion > 16.1 Discretionary Authority
chunks.text: For discretionary accounts, the IMA grants the Firm authority to determine the securities to be bought or sold, the amounts, the broker-dealers used and the timing of transactions without the client's consent for each transaction, subject to the client's guidelines and written restrictions. The Firm may not replace a client's custodian or change the reference index without the client's written consent.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 16. Investment Discretion > 16.2 Non-Discretionary Accounts
chunks.text: For non-discretionary accounts, the Firm recommends transactions and places them only after the client approves each transaction. Because approval may take time, non-discretionary accounts may trade after discretionary accounts, may not participate in aggregated orders and may receive different prices.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 17. Voting Client Securities > 17.1 Proxy and Consent Voting
chunks.text: Where a client has delegated voting authority, the Firm votes proxies and responds to consent solicitations, amendment and waiver requests, exchange offers and bankruptcy plan ballots under its Proxy Voting and Corporate Actions Policy. Because clients hold almost exclusively debt securities, most matters are consent solicitations rather than shareholder proxies. The portfolio manager and the responsible credit analyst recommend a decision, which the Head of Credit Research approves, based on the economic interest of the affected clients as creditors. The Firm does not retain a proxy advisory firm. A material conflict, such as a matter in which clients hold different parts of an issuer's capital structure, is referred to the Chief Compliance Officer, who documents the conflict and the basis for the decision. Clients may obtain the policy and their voting records on request.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 17. Voting Client Securities > 17.2 Class Actions and Bankruptcy Claims
chunks.text: The Firm does not file proofs of claim in securities class actions or bankruptcy proceedings on behalf of separate account clients. Separate account clients and their custodians retain that responsibility, and the Firm forwards to the client any notice it receives. For the Commingled Fund, the Firm identifies eligible claims and files them with the assistance of the Fund's administrator.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 18. Financial Information > 18.1 Financial Condition
chunks.text: The Firm does not require or solicit prepayment of more than $1,200 in fees per client six months or more in advance and therefore is not required to include a balance sheet in this brochure. The Firm is not aware of any financial condition that is reasonably likely to impair its ability to meet contractual commitments to clients, and it has not been the subject of a bankruptcy petition at any time during the past ten years.

chunks.text: # Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures **Wrenholt Pryce Asset Management LLC** Version 2026.1, effective January 15, 2026 Adopted by the Management Committee on January 13, 2026 Policy owner: Priya Castellane, Chief Compliance Officer > **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT: FOR BENCHMARK USE ONLY.** This document is fictional. Wrenholt Pryce Asset Management LLC, Wrenholt Pryce Long Duration Credit Fund, L.P. and all persons, service providers and figures named herein are invented for the purpose of evaluating document-processing systems. It is not an offer to sell securities and does not describe any real entity.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.text: This Compliance Manual (the "Manual") sets out the written policies and procedures that Wrenholt Pryce Asset Management LLC (the "Firm") has adopted under Rule 206(4)-7 under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act") to prevent, detect and correct violations of the Advisers Act and the rules under it. The Code of Ethics in Section 3 and the personal trading, gifts and political contribution procedures in Sections 4 through 6 together constitute the Firm's code of ethics under Rule 204A-1.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE > 1.2 Applicability
chunks.text: "Supervised persons" means all members, officers and employees of the Firm, and any temporary worker, contractor or consultant whom the Chief Compliance Officer ("CCO") designates because the person has access to nonpublic information regarding client holdings or transactions or is engaged for more than 30 days. Every supervised person must read the Manual, certify compliance on hire and annually, and report violations as described in Section 3.3.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE > 1.3 Related Policies and Amendments
chunks.text: The Manual is supplemented by the Valuation Policy and Procedures, the Business Continuity Plan, the Proxy Voting and Corporate Actions Policy and the Information Security Program. Where a supplemental policy addresses a subject in greater detail, that policy governs. Amendments to the Manual are adopted by the Management Committee on the CCO's recommendation. Between scheduled revisions, the CCO may issue a written compliance memorandum, approved by the Management Committee, that amends a provision of the Manual or of any supplemental policy; the memorandum supersedes the affected provision from its effective date until the provision is revised.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE > 1.4 Exceptions
chunks.text: Exceptions to any provision of the Manual must be requested in writing and approved in writing by the CCO, or by the Chief Executive Officer for an exception requested by the CCO. Exceptions are logged and reported to the Management Committee quarterly.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.1 Designation
chunks.text: The Management Committee has designated Priya Castellane as the Firm's CCO. Ms. Castellane has served as CCO since March 2018. Nadia Fenwick serves as Deputy Chief Compliance Officer ("Deputy CCO") and exercises the CCO's authority when the CCO is unavailable or has a conflict. The compliance department consists of the CCO, the Deputy CCO and two compliance analysts.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.2 Reporting Line and Authority
chunks.text: The CCO reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer, Colette Varnum, and has direct and unrestricted access to the Management Committee. The CCO has authority to develop and enforce the Firm's policies and procedures, to access all Firm records and personnel, to retain outside counsel or compliance consultants within the approved compliance budget, and to escalate any matter to the Management Committee without the prior approval of any other officer.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.3 Responsibilities
chunks.text: The CCO is responsible for administering the Manual and the Code of Ethics; maintaining the compliance calendar; overseeing guideline monitoring and resolving exceptions; reviewing personal trading, gifts and political contribution records; approving marketing materials; overseeing regulatory filings, including Form ADV and Form PF; conducting the annual review; and delivering training.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.4 Reporting to Management
chunks.text: The CCO delivers a written compliance report to the Management Committee each quarter covering exceptions, violations, regulatory developments and the status of remediation items, and delivers the annual review report described in Section 15.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.1 Standards of Business Conduct
chunks.text: Supervised persons must act with honesty and integrity and in the best interest of clients; place the interests of clients ahead of their own and those of the Firm; comply with the federal securities laws; avoid conflicts of interest or, where a conflict cannot be avoided, disclose it to the CCO; and keep client information confidential.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.2 Access Persons
chunks.text: All employees are designated access persons. The CCO may designate other supervised persons as access persons.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.3 Reporting Violations
chunks.text: Supervised persons must promptly report any actual or suspected violation of the Code or the Manual to the CCO or, if the matter involves the CCO, to the Chief Executive Officer. Reports may also be made anonymously through the Firm's third-party ethics hotline. The Firm prohibits retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith. The CCO records each reported violation, the investigation performed and the outcome in the violations log.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.4 Sanctions
chunks.text: Violations may result in a written warning, reversal of the transaction, disgorgement of profits, a fine, suspension of personal trading privileges, reduction of discretionary bonus or termination of employment. Disgorged amounts are donated to a charity selected by the Firm. The CCO determines sanctions for employees; sanctions for a member of the Management Committee are determined by the Management Committee without the participation of that member.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.5 Acknowledgments
chunks.text: Each supervised person must acknowledge receipt of the Code within 10 days after hire, annually by January 31, and within 10 business days after receiving any amendment.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.1 Covered Accounts and Covered Securities
chunks.text: "Covered accounts" include every account in which an access person has a direct or indirect beneficial interest, including accounts of a spouse, domestic partner, minor child or other household member, and every account over which the access person has investment discretion. "Covered securities" include all securities except direct obligations of the U.S. government, bankers' acceptances, bank certificates of deposit, commercial paper, high quality short-term debt instruments including repurchase agreements, money market fund shares and shares of open-end funds not advised by the Firm. Interests in the Commingled Fund are covered securities.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.2 Pre-Clearance
chunks.text: Access persons must obtain pre-clearance through the Firm's personal trading platform, provided by Tarnwell Compliance Software, before any transaction in a covered security, including an exchange-traded fund. Compliance reviews each request against the Restricted List, pending and recent client transactions and the restrictions in Section 4.3. The CCO's own requests are reviewed by the Deputy CCO. A pre-clearance approval is valid through the close of regular trading on the business day following the day on which the approval is granted; an order not executed within that period, including an unfilled limit order, must be pre-cleared again. Transactions in an account managed by an unaffiliated adviser over which the access person has no influence or control are exempt from pre-clearance upon written certification to Compliance.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.3 Prohibited and Restricted Transactions
chunks.text: Access persons may not: (a) purchase individual corporate bonds, municipal bonds, asset-backed or mortgage-backed securities, or privately placed debt; (b) trade any security of an issuer on the Restricted List; (c) trade any equity or equity-linked security of an issuer whose debt securities a client account has bought or sold within three business days before or after the transaction (the "blackout period"), and any profit on a transaction later found to fall within the blackout period is subject to disgorgement; (d) acquire securities in an initial public offering; (e) acquire securities in a limited offering, including an interest in the Commingled Fund or any other private fund, without the prior written approval of the CCO; or (f) sell short, or buy put options on, the securities of any issuer whose securities are held in a client account.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.4 Holding Period
chunks.text: Covered securities, other than exchange-traded funds that track broad market indices, must be held for at least 30 calendar days from the date of acquisition. Holding periods are measured on a last-in, first-out basis. The CCO may grant an exception in writing for hardship or for a sale at a loss. Profits realized on a sale in violation of this Section are subject to disgorgement.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.5 Reporting
chunks.text: Each access person must submit an initial holdings report within 10 days after becoming an access person, with information current as of a date no more than 45 days before the person became an access person; a quarterly transaction report within 30 days after the end of each calendar quarter; and an annual holdings report within 30 days after the end of each calendar year, with information current as of a date no more than 45 days before submission. Broker data feeds received in the Tarnwell platform satisfy these requirements if complete. Covered accounts must be held at broker-dealers that provide data feeds unless the CCO approves otherwise.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING AND PRE-CLEARANCE > 4.6 Review
chunks.text: Compliance reviews all reports and pre-clearance activity, compares personal transactions with client trading, and documents its review within 30 days after each report is due. The Deputy CCO reviews the CCO's reports and transactions.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.1 General Principles
chunks.text: Supervised persons may not give or accept any gift, entertainment or other benefit that could reasonably be expected to influence a business decision or create an appearance of impropriety. Cash and cash equivalents, including gift cards, may never be given or accepted. All gifts and entertainment given or received must be recorded in the gifts and entertainment log in the Tarnwell platform within 10 business days.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.2 Gifts Received
chunks.text: Supervised persons may not accept gifts from any single business contact, including any broker-dealer, issuer, vendor or consultant, with an aggregate value exceeding $250 per calendar year. A gift exceeding that limit must be declined or returned or, with the CCO's approval, donated to charity. Promotional items of nominal value bearing a company logo do not count toward the limit but must be logged.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.3 Entertainment
chunks.text: Business entertainment, meaning a meal or event attended by both the supervised person and a representative of the host, is permitted if it is reasonable in value and frequency and has a legitimate business purpose. Entertainment with a value exceeding $500 per person per event requires the prior approval of the CCO. Supervised persons may not accept travel or lodging paid for by a broker-dealer, issuer or vendor; the Firm pays for employee travel to dealer-sponsored conferences and issuer meetings. Traders may not accept entertainment from any single broker-dealer more than four times per calendar year.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.4 Gifts and Entertainment Given
chunks.text: No gift or entertainment may be provided to any trustee, official or employee of a public pension plan client or prospect, or to any other government official, unless the CCO has approved it in advance after confirming that it is permitted under the ethics laws that apply to the recipient. Many state and local ethics codes prohibit public officials from accepting anything of value from an investment manager. Gifts to representatives of insurance company clients, other non-governmental clients, prospects and consultants may not exceed $200 per recipient per calendar year.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.1 Scope
chunks.text: Rule 206(4)-5 under the Advisers Act (the "pay-to-play rule") prohibits an adviser from receiving compensation for advisory services to a government entity for two years after the adviser or a covered associate makes a contribution to an official of that government entity, subject to limited exceptions. Because the Firm's clients include public pension plans and any employee may become a covered associate through a change in responsibilities, the Firm treats every employee as a covered associate for purposes of this Section.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.2 Pre-Clearance and Limits
chunks.text: Every employee must obtain the CCO's written pre-clearance before making any political contribution, regardless of amount, to an incumbent, candidate or successful candidate for state or local office (including a candidate for federal office who currently holds a state or local office), a state or local political party, or a political action committee. The CCO will approve a contribution to an official or candidate only if it does not exceed $350 per election for an official or candidate for whom the employee is entitled to vote, or $150 per election for any other official or candidate. Primary and general elections are separate elections. A contribution by a spouse or household member made at the employee's direction is treated as a contribution by the employee.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.3 Pre-Employment Review
chunks.text: Each candidate for employment must disclose all political contributions made during the two years before the anticipated start date, and the CCO reviews the disclosure before an offer becomes final.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.4 Solicitation, Coordination and Placement Agents
chunks.text: Employees may not solicit or coordinate contributions to an official of a government entity, or payments to a political party of a state or locality, where the Firm provides or seeks to provide advisory services. The Firm does not compensate placement agents or other third parties to solicit government entities.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.5 Records
chunks.text: The CCO maintains a list of government entity clients and government entity investors in the Commingled Fund, records of all contributions pre-cleared and made, and the list of covered associates, as required by Rule 204-2.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.1 Policy
chunks.text: Supervised persons may not trade, for themselves or for any client, while in possession of material nonpublic information ("MNPI"), and may not communicate MNPI to others in violation of law. Information is material if a reasonable investor would consider it important to an investment decision, and nonpublic until it has been disseminated in a manner that makes it available to investors generally. The prohibition applies to debt securities and credit derivatives as well as equity securities.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.2 Sources of MNPI in Fixed Income
chunks.text: Common sources of MNPI at the Firm include due diligence materials for private placements provided under confidentiality agreements; noteholder information provided in connection with amendments, consent solicitations or restructurings; participation in ad hoc creditor committees; and wall-crossing by dealers marketing a new issue before its public announcement.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.3 Wall-Crossing and Private-Side Information
chunks.text: No supervised person may agree to be wall-crossed or accept private-side information without first obtaining the approval of the CCO or the Deputy CCO. When approval is given, Compliance places the issuer on the Restricted List before the information is received and records the persons who received it. The issuer remains on the Restricted List until the CCO determines that the information has become public or is no longer material.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.4 Restricted List and Watch List
chunks.text: Compliance maintains the Restricted List, which is coded in the order management system to block client trades and in the Tarnwell platform to block personal trades. Compliance also maintains a confidential Watch List of issuers about which the Firm may hold sensitive information, which it uses to monitor trading without restricting it.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.5 Expert Networks
chunks.text: The Firm does not engage expert network firms.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING REVIEW > 8.1 Scope
chunks.text: The Firm treats as advertisements subject to Rule 206(4)-1 (the "Marketing Rule") its presentations and pitch books, requests for proposal responses, submissions to investment consultant databases, market commentary distributed to prospects, and website content.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING REVIEW > 8.2 Review and Approval
chunks.text: All marketing materials must be reviewed and approved in writing by the CCO or the Deputy CCO before first use. Before submission to Compliance, the portfolio analytics team verifies every performance figure against the Firm's performance system of record. One-on-one communications with existing clients are generally not advertisements but remain subject to the antifraud provisions of the Advisers Act.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING REVIEW > 8.3 Performance Presentation
chunks.text: Net performance must be presented with at least equal prominence to gross performance, for one, five and ten year periods or since inception if shorter. Extracted performance must be accompanied by, or offered with, the performance of the total portfolio. Hypothetical performance, including projected liability hedge outcomes, may be provided only to institutional recipients with the resources to evaluate it, together with the assumptions and limitations on which it rests.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING REVIEW > 8.4 Testimonials, Endorsements and Third-Party Ratings
chunks.text: The Firm does not use testimonials or endorsements. A third-party rating or ranking may be used only with the disclosures required by the Marketing Rule and the CCO's approval.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE ALLOCATION AND AGGREGATION > 9.1 Aggregation
chunks.text: Portfolio managers may aggregate orders for multiple accounts when aggregation is consistent with the duty to seek best execution and with each account's guidelines. Before an aggregated order is placed, the portfolio manager enters the pre-allocation in the order management system provided by Pelloran Systems. Orders for non-discretionary accounts and trades placed to meet a client's broker utilization goal are not aggregated.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE ALLOCATION AND AGGREGATION > 9.2 Allocation of Partial Fills
chunks.text: If an aggregated order is partially filled, the executed amount is allocated pro rata among participating accounts based on their pre-allocated amounts. Where a pro rata allocation would give an account less than $250,000 par value, or less than the security's minimum denomination, the trader may reallocate that amount pro rata among the other participating accounts. Each participating account receives the average price.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE ALLOCATION AND AGGREGATION > 9.3 New Issues
chunks.text: Indications of interest for a new issue must be entered by account in the order management system before the order book closes. The allotment received is allocated pro rata to those indications, and any adjustment for guideline constraints or cash availability is documented by the portfolio manager.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE ALLOCATION AND AGGREGATION > 9.4 Departures from Pre-Allocation
chunks.text: Any allocation that departs from the pre-allocation requires a written explanation by the portfolio manager and the approval of the CCO or the Deputy CCO before the end of the trade date.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE ALLOCATION AND AGGREGATION > 9.5 Review
chunks.text: Compliance reviews the allocation of all aggregated orders monthly and, with the Chief Risk Officer, reviews performance dispersion among accounts in each strategy quarterly.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION REVIEW > 10.1 Standard
chunks.text: The Firm seeks to execute each transaction on the most favorable terms reasonably available under the circumstances. For fixed income securities traded with dealers as principal, the net price is the principal factor, considered together with size, liquidity, market conditions, settlement capability and the counterparty's financial condition.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION REVIEW > 10.2 Best Execution Committee
chunks.text: The Best Execution Committee is chaired by the Chief Operating Officer, Dmitri Halloway. Its other members are the Head of Trading, Marcus Ebbing; the Chief Risk Officer, Yuki Ashbury; the Director of Portfolio Operations, Leopold Sarkis; and the CCO. A majority of members constitutes a quorum.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION REVIEW > 10.3 Meetings and Review Data
chunks.text: The Committee meets quarterly. At each meeting it reviews transaction cost analysis prepared by Orrinmoor Analytics, which compares each execution with the evaluated price supplied by the primary pricing service at the time of trade and with composite dealer quotations; the number of competitive quotations obtained, against a target of at least three quotations for investment grade trades over $1 million par when market conditions permit; the share of volume executed with each dealer and through each electronic platform; settlement failures; and use of minority-owned, women-owned and veteran-owned broker-dealers against client goals. Minutes record the Committee's conclusions and any follow-up.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION REVIEW > 10.4 Approved Counterparty List
chunks.text: A new dealer may be added to the approved counterparty list only with the Committee's approval after review of its financial condition and settlement capability. The list is reviewed annually, and the Chief Risk Officer may suspend a counterparty immediately for credit reasons.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.1 Governance
chunks.text: The Chief Technology Officer, Samuel Treloar, serves as the Firm's Information Security Officer ("ISO") and is responsible for the Information Security Program. The ISO conducts an annual cybersecurity risk assessment and reports on the program to the Management Committee quarterly.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.2 Technical Controls
chunks.text: The Firm requires multi-factor authentication for all remote and privileged access; encrypts data at rest and in transit; grants access on a least-privilege basis and reviews entitlements quarterly; and deploys endpoint detection and response software on all Firm devices. Grisby Lane Security provides managed security services, including monitoring by its security operations center 24 hours a day. Vulnerability scans are performed monthly. An external penetration test is performed annually by a qualified independent firm that is not otherwise engaged to provide managed security services to the Firm, and the ISO tracks each finding to remediation.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.3 Vendor Oversight
chunks.text: Vendors with access to Firm systems or confidential information are reviewed before engagement and annually thereafter, including review of available SOC 1 or SOC 2 reports, security questionnaires and contractual breach notification terms.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual: Policies and Procedures, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 11. CYBERSECURITY AND INFORMATION SECURITY > 11.4 Incident Reporting and Response
chunks.text: Any supervised person who suspects an information security incident must report it to the ISO and the CCO immediately, and in any event within one hour after discovery. The ISO leads the response under Section 9 of the Business Continuity Plan, and notifications to affected individuals are made under Section 12.4.

chunks.text: # Valuation Policy and Procedures **Wrenholt Pryce Asset Management LLC** Effective February 10, 2026 Approved by the Management Committee on February 10, 2026 Policy owner: Ines Morrow-Tate, Chief Financial Officer and Chair of the Valuation Committee > **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT: FOR BENCHMARK USE ONLY.** This document is fictional. Wrenholt Pryce Asset Management LLC, Wrenholt Pryce Long Duration Credit Fund, L.P. and all persons, service providers and figures named herein are invented for the purpose of evaluating document-processing systems. It is not an offer to sell securities and does not describe any real entity.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.text: This Policy establishes the procedures by which Wrenholt Pryce Asset Management LLC (the "Firm") determines the fair value of investments held in the accounts it manages. Values determined under this Policy are used to calculate the net asset value of Wrenholt Pryce Long Duration Credit Fund, L.P. (the "Commingled Fund") and to prepare its financial statements, to calculate management fees, and to prepare client and performance reports. Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date, consistent with ASC Topic 820.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE > 1.2 Scope
chunks.text: This Policy applies to every position held in the Commingled Fund and in each separate account. For separate accounts, the client's custodian maintains the official book of record. Portfolio Operations reconciles the Firm's values to custodian values monthly and investigates any account-level difference greater than 0.10% of account market value.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE > 1.3 Valuation Time
chunks.text: Positions are valued as of 4:00 p.m. Eastern time on each business day. Month-end values are finalized by Portfolio Operations by the fifth business day after month end and are subject to review by the Valuation Committee at its next meeting.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.1 Composition
chunks.text: The voting members of the Valuation Committee (the "Committee") are the Chief Financial Officer, Ines Morrow-Tate, who chairs the Committee; the Chief Risk Officer, Yuki Ashbury; and the Director of Portfolio Operations, Leopold Sarkis. The Chief Compliance Officer, Priya Castellane, and the Head of Credit Research, Rafael Denholm, attend as non-voting members. Portfolio managers and traders are not members; they may be invited to provide market information but leave the meeting before any vote.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.2 Quorum and Voting
chunks.text: A quorum consists of two voting members, at least one of whom must be the Chief Financial Officer or the Chief Risk Officer. Decisions require the vote of a majority of the voting members present. Members may participate by video or telephone. For a time-sensitive matter, the Committee may act by unanimous written consent of the voting members, which is ratified at the next meeting.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.3 Meetings
chunks.text: The Committee meets monthly, within 10 business days after each month end, and at any other time at the request of any member. Portfolio Operations prepares the minutes, which the Chief Compliance Officer reviews.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.4 Responsibilities
chunks.text: The Committee approves pricing sources and valuation methodologies; reviews Level 3 positions, price challenge logs, override reports, stale price reports and back-testing results; approves fair value determinations; and reports quarterly to the Management Committee on valuation matters, including any material change in methodology.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.5 Conflicts of Interest
chunks.text: Because management fees and reported performance depend on the values determined under this Policy, the Firm has an incentive to overstate values. The Committee addresses this conflict by vesting pricing responsibility in Portfolio Operations, which reports to the Chief Financial Officer and not to the Chief Investment Officer, by excluding portfolio managers and traders from its votes, and by the independent review described in Section 8. A voting member who has a personal interest in a matter before the Committee must disclose it and abstain.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.1 Hierarchy
chunks.text: Each position is valued using the first available source in the following order: (1) for exchange-traded instruments, the official settlement or closing price on the primary exchange; (2) the evaluated price supplied by the primary pricing service; (3) the evaluated price supplied by the secondary pricing service, where the primary service does not cover the security or its price has been rejected under Section 5; (4) broker quotations obtained under Section 3.4; and (5) a fair value determined by the Committee under Section 4.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.2 Primary Pricing Service
chunks.text: Lanthorn Evaluated Pricing, Inc. is the primary pricing service for all fixed income securities held by the Firm's clients, including U.S. Treasury and agency securities, agency mortgage-backed pools and to-be-announced contracts, corporate and taxable municipal bonds, and asset-backed and commercial mortgage-backed securities. Long positions are valued at the service's bid-side evaluation as of 4:00 p.m. Eastern time.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.3 Secondary Pricing Service
chunks.text: Brayford Pricing Data LLC is the secondary pricing service. Its evaluations are used for the daily tolerance comparison in Section 5.1 and as the pricing source for any security that Lanthorn Evaluated Pricing does not cover or whose Lanthorn price has been rejected.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.4 Broker Quotations
chunks.text: When neither pricing service provides a reliable price, Portfolio Operations, and not the trading desk, obtains bid-side quotations from dealers. At least two independent dealer quotations are required. Where two are obtained, the position is valued at their average; where three or more are obtained, at their median. A price based on a single quotation is a Level 3 valuation and requires the approval of the Committee.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.5 Instrument-Specific Sources
chunks.text: Treasury futures are valued at the exchange settlement price. Cleared interest rate swaps are valued at the end-of-day settlement valuation published by the clearing house. Money market fund shares are valued at their reported net asset value. Privately placed notes are valued under Section 4.2.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.6 New Issues
chunks.text: A newly issued security is valued at its offering price until the primary pricing service begins coverage. If coverage has not begun by the second business day after settlement, Portfolio Operations obtains broker quotations under Section 3.4 or requests coverage from the secondary pricing service.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.1 Classification
chunks.text: At each month end, Portfolio Operations classifies each position in the fair value hierarchy. Level 1 includes exchange-traded futures and on-the-run Treasury securities; Level 2 includes securities valued at evaluated prices derived from observable inputs; and Level 3 includes positions valued using significant unobservable inputs, including single broker quotations, the private placement matrix and distressed recovery models. Transfers between levels are reported to the Committee.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.2 Privately Placed Notes
chunks.text: Privately placed notes are valued by a matrix method. The Firm determines a spread over the interpolated U.S. Treasury curve equal to the spread of comparable public securities of the same issuer or, where none exist, of comparable issuers with a similar internal rating, sector and maturity, plus an illiquidity premium, plus adjustments for structural features such as financial covenants, make-whole provisions, security and subordination. The note's scheduled cash flows are discounted at the resulting yield. The illiquidity premium is set by the Committee quarterly and currently ranges from 15 to 40 basis points depending on issue size and structure.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.3 Distressed and Defaulted Securities
chunks.text: Securities of an issuer that is in default, or that is assigned the lowest internal rating categories, are valued using a recovery analysis based on the estimated enterprise value available to each class of creditors or on recovery rates observed in comparable restructurings. The recovery value is compared with any available dealer quotations, and differences are explained in the valuation memorandum.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.4 Documentation and Approval
chunks.text: Each Level 3 valuation is supported by a valuation memorandum that records the inputs, their sources and the rationale for each judgment. Level 3 valuations are approved by the Committee at its monthly meeting. For the Commingled Fund's financial statements, Portfolio Operations prepares the quantitative disclosure of significant unobservable inputs.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 5.1 Tolerance Checks
chunks.text: Each business day, Portfolio Operations compares the primary and secondary evaluations for every security. A difference of more than 1.0 point (1% of par) for an investment grade security, or more than 2.0 points for a below investment grade or structured security, is investigated on the same business day. Portfolio Operations also investigates any day-over-day price change of more than 2.0 points for an investment grade security, or 5.0 points for any other security, that is not explained by a market event.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 5.2 Price Challenges
chunks.text: When Portfolio Operations concludes that a vendor price does not reflect fair value, based on evidence such as recent reported trades, executable dealer quotations or new issue pricing, it submits a formal challenge through the vendor's challenge process within one business day. Each challenge is recorded in the challenge log. If the vendor does not respond within three business days, or declines to change its price, the matter is escalated to the Chief Financial Officer.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 5.3 Overrides
chunks.text: A price override, meaning the use of a price other than the price indicated by the hierarchy in Section 3.1, must be approved in writing by the Chief Financial Officer before it is applied. Portfolio Operations prepares each override request with the supporting evidence. Overrides are reported to the Committee at its next meeting and lapse at that meeting unless the Committee re-approves them.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 5.4 Role of Portfolio Managers and Traders
chunks.text: Portfolio managers and traders may provide market information to Portfolio Operations and may ask it to challenge a price, but they may not communicate with pricing vendors about the valuation of positions they manage, determine a price, or approve an override.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. STALE PRICE MONITORING > 6.1 Stale Price Threshold
chunks.text: Portfolio Operations runs a stale price report each business day. A security whose price from its assigned source has not changed for five consecutive business days is flagged as stale. For each flagged security, Portfolio Operations obtains dealer quotations or other market evidence to confirm or replace the price and records the result.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. STALE PRICE MONITORING > 6.2 Escalation
chunks.text: A security whose price remains unchanged for 20 consecutive business days is referred to the Committee, which determines whether the price should be replaced by a fair value determination. The Committee receives a monthly summary of all stale price flags and their resolution.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. BACK-TESTING > 7.1 Procedure
chunks.text: Each month, Portfolio Operations compares the valuation of each security sold during the month, as of the business day before the sale, with the actual sale price. Differences are summarized by sector, pricing source and fair value level. Any difference greater than 2.0 points for an investment grade security, or 3.0 points for any other security, is investigated and explained.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. BACK-TESTING > 7.2 Reporting
chunks.text: Back-testing results are reported to the Committee quarterly. A persistent bias in the prices supplied by a source is referred for review of that source and is considered in the annual pricing vendor due diligence under Section 8.3.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW > 8.1 Independent Valuation Firm
chunks.text: Selwick Harrow Valuation Advisors LLC performs an independent review of Level 3 positions each quarter. The review covers every Level 3 position held by the Commingled Fund and every Level 3 position in a separate account with a market value above $10 million. Selwick Harrow provides a range of values for each position reviewed; where the Firm's value falls outside the range, the Committee documents its conclusion and the reasons for it.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW > 8.2 Annual Audit
chunks.text: The Commingled Fund's independent auditor, Marrick Tolland LLP, audits the Fund's valuations as part of its annual audit. Portfolio Operations provides the auditor with the valuation memoranda, challenge logs and Committee minutes it requests.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW > 8.3 Pricing Vendor Due Diligence
chunks.text: The Committee conducts due diligence on each pricing service at least annually, including a review of the vendor's methodology documentation, coverage, responsiveness to challenges, back-testing results and SOC 1 report.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated February 10, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW > 8.4 Policy Review
chunks.text: The Committee and the Chief Compliance Officer review this Policy at least annually. Changes are approved by the Management Committee.

chunks.section: SECTION 5. DATA BACKUP > 5.1 Replication
chunks.text: Systems hosted in the Windsor facility are replicated to the Ferrowby Cloud Backup recovery environment every 15 minutes. In a disruption affecting the Windsor facility, the Chief Technology Officer directs failover to that environment.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 5. DATA BACKUP > 5.2 Backup Frequency, Location and Retention
chunks.text: Nightly immutable backups of all Firm-hosted systems, cloud email and cloud document storage are taken at 11:00 p.m. Eastern time and written to Ferrowby Cloud Backup data centers in Columbus, Ohio and Hillsboro, Oregon. Backups are encrypted using AES-256 and cannot be altered or deleted during their retention period. Nightly backups are retained for 35 days, weekly backups for 13 months, and month-end backups for seven years.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 5. DATA BACKUP > 5.3 Restoration Checks
chunks.text: Technology staff restore a sample of files and one complete system from backup each quarter and document the results, including the time required.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 6. TESTING > 6.1 Testing Program
chunks.text: The Firm conducts a full test of the Plan annually, in the fourth quarter, including relocation of trading and operations staff to the alternate site, remote operation by all other staff, and failover of the Windsor systems to the Ferrowby Cloud Backup recovery environment. Tabletop exercises are conducted semi-annually, at least one of which addresses a cyber incident. The call tree is tested quarterly.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 6. TESTING > 6.2 Most Recent Full Test
chunks.text: The most recent full test was conducted on Saturday, October 18, 2025. Twelve employees operated from the alternate site and the remainder worked remotely, and the Windsor systems were failed over to the recovery environment and restored. All critical systems were restored within their recovery time objectives. The test identified one issue: market data entitlements at the alternate site had not been updated for two traders hired in 2025. The entitlements were corrected in November 2025, and the Coordinator now confirms entitlements monthly.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 6. TESTING > 6.3 Other Exercises
chunks.text: The most recent tabletop exercise, held in June 2025, simulated a ransomware attack affecting the Windsor facility and included Grisby Lane Security and Quenby Digital Forensics LLC. In the call tree test conducted in September 2025, all but two employees acknowledged the notification within the required 30 minutes; both were reached by their department heads.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 6. TESTING > 6.4 Reporting
chunks.text: Results of each test and exercise are reported in writing to the Management Committee and the Chief Compliance Officer, and remediation items are tracked by the Coordinator until closed.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 7. COMMUNICATION TREE > 7.1 Initial Notification
chunks.text: On declaration of a business disruption, the Coordinator sends an emergency notification to all employees through Callowmere Notify by text message, voice call and email. Each employee must acknowledge the notification within 30 minutes.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 7. COMMUNICATION TREE > 7.2 Call Tree
chunks.text: The Chief Operating Officer notifies the Crisis Management Team. Each member then notifies the department heads for which the member is responsible: the Chief Executive Officer notifies the Management Committee and client service; the Chief Investment Officer notifies portfolio management and credit research; the Head of Trading notifies the trading desk; the Chief Financial Officer notifies finance and Portfolio Operations; the Chief Technology Officer notifies technology staff; and the Chief Compliance Officer notifies compliance staff and outside counsel. Department heads call any employee who has not acknowledged the initial notification.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 7. COMMUNICATION TREE > 7.3 External Communications
chunks.text: Client service notifies separate account clients and Commingled Fund investors whose services are affected by the end of the business day on which the disruption is declared. Portfolio Operations notifies custodians, Quillfield Fund Services LLC and key dealers. The Chief Compliance Officer determines whether any regulatory notification is required. Only the Chief Executive Officer may speak to the media.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 8. PANDEMIC AND PUBLIC HEALTH EVENTS > 8.1 Phased Response
chunks.text: In Phase 1 (monitoring), the Crisis Management Team monitors public health guidance and confirms that all employees can work remotely. In Phase 2 (split operations), the trading desk and Portfolio Operations are divided into two teams that alternate weekly between the Hartford office and remote or alternate site operation, so that the teams do not share premises. In Phase 3 (full remote), all employees work remotely and the office is closed except for essential access approved by the Chief Operating Officer.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 8. PANDEMIC AND PUBLIC HEALTH EVENTS > 8.2 Minimum Staffing
chunks.text: Each business day the Firm must have available at least two traders, one portfolio manager for each strategy and two Portfolio Operations analysts. Cross-training records maintained by department heads identify the employees qualified to perform each critical function.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 9. CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 9.1 Incident Response Team
chunks.text: The Incident Response Team is led by the Information Security Officer and includes the Chief Operating Officer, the Chief Compliance Officer, the Chief Financial Officer and the manager of technology operations. Outside counsel joins the team for any incident that may involve unauthorized access to client or personal information.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 9. CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 9.2 Detection and Escalation
chunks.text: Grisby Lane Security monitors the Firm's systems 24 hours a day and escalates any Severity 1 incident, meaning an incident that affects trading, client data or the integrity of Firm systems, to the Information Security Officer by telephone within 15 minutes of detection. Severity 2 and Severity 3 incidents are escalated through the managed security ticketing system.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 9. CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 9.3 Outside Advisers
chunks.text: Quenby Digital Forensics LLC is retained to provide forensic investigation services. Dunmore Achterberg LLP serves as outside counsel for cyber incidents and engages the forensic firm where appropriate so that its work is performed at the direction of counsel.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 9. CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 9.4 Containment and Recovery
chunks.text: The Incident Response Team isolates affected systems, preserves evidence and restores systems from immutable backups under Section 5 after the Information Security Officer confirms that the backups are free of compromise. No ransom may be paid without the approval of the Management Committee after consultation with outside counsel and notification of law enforcement.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated December 1, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 9. CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 9.5 Notifications
chunks.text: The Chief Compliance Officer determines what notifications are required to clients, regulators and affected individuals, including notifications under the privacy provisions of the Compliance Manual. The Chief Financial Officer notifies the Firm's cyber liability insurer in accordance with the terms of the policy.
